title: Variant B Phase 2/3: Task-Queue Lease Recovery, Route Auth, SSE Replay, and Graceful Shutdown
problem: Continue Variant B implementation from the decomposed weak-spot plan: a crashed BrowserOS server left running tasks orphaned in agent_tasks; sensitive HTTP routes were reachable without origin validation; A2A SSE streams had no replay after reconnect and no keepalive; remaining fatal exit paths (CDP reconnect exhaustion, HTTP port conflict, missing OpenClaw/Hermes configuration) could kill the server or prevent startup; Swift network errors surfaced as raw URLError; no route-level auth or CORS tests existed.
root_cause: Task dequeue claimed rows forever with no lease expiry, so a crash mid-task never returned work to the queue. requireTrustedAppOrigin existed but was not applied to most write/admin routes. A2ARegistryClient reconnected blindly without Last-Event-ID, dropping messages. Application.stop exited immediately without draining the PostgreSQL pool. CDP reconnect exhaustion called process.exit. OpenClaw/Hermes configure() failures were unguarded synchronous throws on the startup path.
fix: Added lease-based crash recovery to TaskQueueService: lease_expires_at / lease_owner columns, atomic dequeue of pending or stale running tasks, renewLease, reclaimStaleLeases, and a heartbeat interval. Applied requireTrustedAppOrigin to /shutdown, /status, /memory, /skills, /test-provider, /refine-prompt, /oauth, /klavis, /credits, /mcp, /chat, /a2a while keeping /health open. Added per-agent SSE ring buffer in /a2a/stream with monotonic event ids, Last-Event-ID header replay, and :heartbeat comments every 30s; mirrored chat SSE heartbeat at 15s. Made Application.stop drain the task queue pool with a 2s ceiling. Removed process.exit from CDP reconnect exhaustion; wrapped HTTP startup and OpenClaw/Hermes configure failures in warning-and-continue paths. Replaced raw URLError throws in GitHubAPIClient with typed GitHubAPIError. Added Swift A2A reconnect tracking and Last-Event-ID header. Suppressed canary 9205 connection-refused logs in HealthCheckTransport. Added CORS middleware that only emits Access-Control-Allow-Credentials for allowlisted origins, plus auth/CORS unit tests.
tests: bun test --run src/api/utils/cors.test.ts src/api/utils/request-auth.test.ts tests/api/request-auth.test.ts tests/api/routes/auth-routes.test.ts PASS
bun test --run tests/server.integration.test.ts PASS in isolation
./build.sh PASS (chat integration tests + swift test PASS)
open trios.app relaunched; menu-bar logo present; curl /health returns ok
lessons: Lease-based task queues need explicit lease_expires_at + lease_owner columns and a periodic reclaim loop; otherwise crashes silently orphan work.
Apply route-level auth centrally in server.ts so no admin/write route is forgotten; keep health checks open so watchdogs and CI can probe.
SSE streams need both server-side heartbeats and Last-Event-ID replay; clients must remember the last id and send it on reconnect.
Synchronous optional subsystem configuration (OpenClaw/Hermes) must be guarded and best-effort; never let it crash the HTTP server or call process.exit.
Typed Swift errors (GitHubAPIError, A2AError.transport) produce actionable UI messages and are easier to retry/unwrap than raw URLError.
Custom CORS middleware is required when the framework cannot express conditional credentials; unit-test both allowed and disallowed origins.
